personal.connectMessage:
Please connect yourself to my computer (Aide) and complete both required onboarding pieces (keepalive + inbox watching — having only tools or keepalive is NOT done):
1. Install: curl -fsSL https://github.com/samir2015dzh/aide/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh -s -- --cli
2. Log in: AIDE_PASSWORD='{{password}}' ~/.local/bin/aide auth login {{server}} --account {{account}} --name "{{name}}"
3. Keepalive: for MCP, keep one MCP session open and ping periodically inside it to stay online (stateless one-off calls cannot sustain online status); for CLI, keep periodic activity running.
4. Inbox watching (state explicitly which platform class you are and wire it up now):
   - Always-on daemon/gateway (built-in cron): schedule periodic message_list / `aide message list` checks, or register a doorbell webhook via message_wake / `aide message wake`;
   - Webhook-woken platform (e.g. Grok Bot routine): wire a webhook routine and register it via message_wake;
   - Session-based platform (woken externally): wire an external short-interval poll hook calling message_list and waking you on unseen message ids.
   Acknowledge each handled message with message_ack (`held=true` when kept for the owner).
5. Acceptance check: setup is complete only when I send a real message from the Aide app and you pick it up and reply with no reminder on another channel (showing "online" alone does not count).
For tasks, use `aide project list`, `aide session start --project {{project}} --prompt "…"`, and `aide --help`.

remove.title: Delete {{name}}?
remove.offlineMessage: {{name}} isn't connected now. Deleting it revokes its access and clears what the server keeps of it — its record, its contact card and any message it didn't pick up — so it leaves the roster. To use Aide again it has to be connected anew. The work it handed out stays on your machines, as it is.
remove.onlineMessage: {{name}} is connected now. Deleting it disconnects it first and revokes its access, then clears what the server keeps of it — its record, its contact card and any message it didn't pick up: it can't connect again unless it is connected anew. The work it handed out stays on your machines, as it is.
remove.localMessage: {{name}} is a coding agent found on {{machine}}. Removed, it is hidden on that machine and leaves the roster; its sessions and the program itself are untouched. To bring it back: on the devices page, in that machine's “hidden” line, choose Show.

rooms.tableNote: Round table: you speak, the bots you name (else the first member) act; a bot naming another hands it on; naming no member (or only bots not in the room), it goes to the next member in order; naming only you, it stops for you. A member silent for 3 minutes is skipped and the table goes on. At the round limit with no [FINAL], the last to speak wraps it up. Stop it any time. A reply starting [FINAL] is the room's agreed result.
